Research

Interactions. Knowledge. Adaptation.

My work connects social relationships in recommender systems with knowledge transfer and the interpretation of learning models.

01

Recommendation & social influence

Learning from social interactions

How do trust, influence, and leadership shape collective preferences? My research models relationships between individuals to support personalized and group recommendation.

My published work investigates implicit trust-network construction, influence-aware group recommendation, leader impact, and adaptive group formation through multi-agent reinforcement learning. Applications include e-commerce and multi-day tourist itineraries.

Recommender systemsTrust networksMulti-agent reinforcement learning
02

Knowledge distillation & geometry

Transferring knowledge efficiently

How can a smaller model learn the most useful information from a larger one? I explore geometric alignment, optimal transport, and selective teacher supervision.

Current manuscripts investigate Wasserstein-based distribution alignment, student-calibrated teacher supervision, and budgeted distillation. These directions examine the relationship between representation geometry and the cost of knowledge transfer.

Knowledge distillationOptimal transportRepresentation geometry
03

Causal analysis & language models

Understanding and adapting models

Which internal components matter for a given input? My recent research explores mechanistic interpretability and causally informed adaptation of large language models.

The CRAT manuscript studies causally routed adaptive tuning for machine translation. Related interests include parameter-efficient fine-tuning, probabilistic graphical models, graph neural networks, and uncertainty-aware learning.

Causal interpretabilityLarge language modelsParameter-efficient fine-tuning
